title: Regulatory Amendment Mechanism for Customs and Tax Notifications
summary: The mechanism for amending tax notifications evolved from relying on the Customs Act, 1969 and the VAT Act, 1991 to incorporating the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012, and eventually the Customs Act, 2023. The process consistently involves the government, in the public interest and in consultation with the National Board of Revenue, issuing SROs to modify specific H.S. Codes, descriptions, or rates within existing notification schedules.

evolution.legal_basis: Shifted from Customs Act 1969/VAT Act 1991 to Customs Act 1969/VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012, and finally to Customs Act 2023/VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
evolution.scope: Continuous refinement of H.S. Codes, product descriptions, and tax rates through iterative SRO amendments.

timeline.change: Initial baseline using Customs Act 1969 and VAT Act 1991.
Adjustment of tax rates (from 3% to 5%) within existing notification frameworks.
Transition to legal basis citing VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012.
Adoption of Customs Act, 2023 as the primary legal authority for amendments.
